I built the same board pack twice in one month, and the second one was not a
revision. It was the same work again.

The volume, since this pillar does not get to run on opinion: eleven hours the
first time, nine the second, across three weeks in March. Twenty hours out of
a three day month, and the last nine of them spent producing a document that
already existed.

The result was that the company went into its board meeting with a pack
assembled the night before, and I went into it having done nine hours of
work I could not bill in good conscience.

The cause is the boring one. I built the first pack against the plan the
founder and I had agreed in January. Between January and March the company had
changed how it counted a qualified pipeline, and nobody thought to tell me,
because to them it was a sales operations change and not a finance change. It
was not a finance change. It was a definition change, and a definition change
invalidates every chart built on the old one.

I want to be precise about the failure, because it is mine. I had no standing
way of hearing about it. I was in the company three days a month and I had
built no seam that would carry a change like that to me between visits.

So in April I wrote one line into the working agreement of every mandate: any
change to how the company counts a customer, a qualified lead, or a recognised
euro comes to me the week it is decided, not the month it is reported. It is
one sentence and it sits above the fee.

It has been triggered twice since. Both times the message was two lines long
and both times it saved a day of my work and a night of theirs.

Nadia Feriel, fractional CFO for seed and Series A B2B SaaS.
I build the model and I sit in the room when it gets argued about.
